newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower but most losses pared.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower but most losses pared.

text.p: COMEX copper clawed its way back up by the close to regain much of the ground ceded early in the session when prices slid on profit-taking despite a dip in LME stocks.
LME inventory on Friday fell 3,475 tonnes to 216,575 tonnes, in line with trade expectations. Stocks are still considerably higher than at the beginning of the year.
Most active May copper settled 0.45 cent weaker at 110.90 cents per pound, traded 111.35 to 109.25 cents. Spot March went out 0.20 cent down at 113.75 cents.
Volume was less than half the lots traded in the previous two sessions as the rollover from March to May slowed.
May settled 1.20 cents up on the week, with March up 0.45 cent.

"The market has proved to be quite resilient, but it seems to be more technically guided than anything else," John Gross of the Copper Journal said. "I believe the price has gone a bit ahead of fundamentals."

Nevertheless, with spot March breaking through 112.00 cents, it was set to target 120 cents before moving lower, Gross added. Demand was still strong in the U.S., though the building wire sector was not as buoyant as it has been.
During the session the LME backwardation rose some $5 to $55/$60, helping the markets pare their losses.
